name: drop_in_place
documentation:
Executes the destructor (if any) of the pointed-to value.

 See [`ptr::drop_in_place`] for safety concerns and examples.

 [`ptr::drop_in_place`]: crate::ptr::drop_in_place()
rules: `self` must be valid for both reads and writes.
`self` must be properly aligned, even if `T` has size 0; an unaligned value must be copied to an aligned location before being dropped.
`self` must be nonnull, even if `T` has size 0.
The value pointed to by `self` must be valid for dropping, including any additional invariants required by its type.
While `drop_in_place` is executing, parts of the value pointed to by `self` may be accessed only through the `&mut self` references supplied to the `Drop::drop` methods it invokes.
If `T` is not `Copy`, using the pointed-to value after calling `drop_in_place` can cause undefined behavior; assigning with `*self = foo` counts as a use because it drops the value again.
After calling `drop_in_place`, `write()` may be used to overwrite the pointed-to data without dropping it again.
`drop_in_place` may be used to drop pinned data when `T` is not `repr(packed)`; pinned data must not be moved before it is dropped.
